subject: MAP kickoff: Nimbus POC — unit-econ assumptions & eval timeline
messages:
From: Tom Sayers <tom.sayers@nimbus.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@nimbus.com>, procurement@nimbus.com
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: Nimbus POC unit economics & eval timeline

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the intro call today. Nimbus is excited to move the POC forward. Before we lock dates, procurement and engineering asked for a short MAP that calls out the unit-econ assumptions (tokens / $), caching & batching expectations, and a proposed evaluation plan so we can scope budget and timelines. High-level asks from our side:

- Target close: end of May (ideally 2028-05-31)
- Expected steady-state QPS for chat/assistant flows: ~15 rps peak, ~5 rps avg
- Latency SLO: 500ms 95th
- Primary questions: what tokens/$ should we budget for (with/without KV caching), how batching impacts latency and cost in your hosted offering, and what fallback model options are at different price points.

Can you share a short doc / spreadsheet with the MAP + cost model and a suggested evaluation timeline? Procurement will use that to draft the purchase requisition.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Sayers
Head of Platforms, Nimbus Health

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sayers <tom.sayers@nimbus.com>
Cc: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@nimbus.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, procurement@nimbus.com
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: Nimbus POC unit economics & eval timeline

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a cost workbook (see attachment). Quick summary of the assumptions in the sheet (tab: unit-econ-summary):

- Baseline model: redwood-gpt-medium (fp16) -> baseline token price: $0.0009 / 1k tokens (hosted)
- Quantized variant (int8) option: ~20% cost savings vs baseline, recommended for high-throughput routes
- KV prefix caching: for assistant flows with repeated context, expect 30–50% token reduction (depends on prompt reuse)
- Batching: at 50–200ms batching windows we see 10–30% token-cost improvement for small messages; at >200ms batching gives diminishing latency returns and higher tail latency
- Suggested pilot config: 2 model routes (low-cost quantized + high-quality fp16), enable per-route prefix cache for FAQ/autocomplete routes, 100ms batching window for async enrichment jobs, and 40ms for conversational low-latency route

Attached: nimbus_map_unit_econ_v1.xlsx (cols: scenario, tokens_per_call, calls_per_min, batching_ms, cache_hit_rate, estimated_tokens_per_day, monthly_cost_est)

Eval plan attached (nimbus_eval_plan_v1.md) with proposed prompt sets and pass/fail criteria tied to token budget and latency gates. Proposed timeline inside: demo + eval dataset run in weeks 1–2, procurement review week 3, pilot rollout week 4, target close week 8.

Next steps: if these assumptions look reasonable, I'm happy to join a procurement call to review the workbook live and walk through tradeoffs.

Best —
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: nimbus_map_unit_econ_v1.xlsx (Excel)]
[Attachment: nimbus_eval_plan_v1.md (markdown)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Sayers <tom.sayers@nimbus.com>, Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@nimbus.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: Nimbus POC unit economics & eval timeline

Looping in a couple quick internal clarifications before we present to Nimbus:

- Cache hit assumptions: we should show a conservative (20%), expected (35%), and optimistic (50%) column in the workbook so procurement can see ranges.
- Quantization impact: for models with long context (>2k tokens) int8 can reduce memory pressure but may increase latency slightly; note both perf and quality tradeoffs in the comments column.
- Batching windows: suggest adding a latency tradeoff table: 0–50ms (near real-time), 50–150ms (acceptable for async chat but better throughput), >150ms (only for bulk jobs).

I updated the draft workbook and added an "assumption_notes" tab. Alex — can you share the Drive link in the next thread and propose two demo slots next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solution Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@nimbus.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Sayers <tom.sayers@nimbus.com>, procurement@nimbus.com
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: Nimbus POC unit economics & eval timeline

Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed workbook. Procurement likes seeing the range columns — that helped. A couple quick confirmations from Nimbus: 

- We will budget to the conservative column for initial purchase and leave an uplift for caching gains during the pilot.
- Pilot scope approved: run main prompt set against both model routes for 2 weeks (Week A: fp16 baseline; Week B: quantized route). We'll measure tokens/day, average latency, and quality metrics you propose.
- Demo slots: Tue 2028-04-16 10:00am PT or Thu 2028-04-18 2:00pm PT — either works for the team.

Procurement flagged one ask: can you provide a short one-pager describing fallback behavior if the dedicated route is at capacity (e.g., auto-failover to lower-cost variant and expected latency impact)? If you can add that to the MAP spreadsheet we can move to PR creation next week.

If all good, we'll aim to finalize PO and terms by the week of 2028-04-23 and kick pilot the following week to keep the May close target realistic.

Regards,
Lena Brooks
Sr. Program Manager, Nimbus Health
[Accepted attachment: nimbus_map_unit_econ_v1.xlsx]
